author: PokerFace
body:
Part 1: About You

What is your age?
-17

What is your Discord ID? (If you don’t have Discord, create an account and join the Avicus Discord server before answering this question.)
-PokerFace#2575

How active can you be in order to contribute to the team?
-I can contribute to every single discussion related to the development of maps and concepts. Regarding map-making, I can probably finish 1 map on my own every now and then as well as contributing to joint builder/map developer projects. When I work with someone else, we can finish in a matter of days.

What attributes distinguish yourself from other applicants that qualify you to be a builder?
-Being a long time player in the competitive scene, I can analyze maps and determine what changes could make gameplay more enjoyable. I also like to add a unique concept to the maps I make, such as incorporating redstone elevators. I also pay a lot of attention to fine detail such as symmetricity and just adding a few decorations here and there. I also like to make sure everything is fully optimized. For example, if I were to become a builder, some things I would do is fix loadouts, because lots of loadouts have wooden planks on the remove-drop list which is very annoying for players. I do not have a lot of experience with XML, but I can just fill in the blank and at least I know I am making a difference.

Part 2: Skills

What do you think is a necessity in order to hone your map building skills in terms of gameplay?
-I think one thing that will help for sure is taking a look at some of the most favorited tournament maps of Avicus. Examples of these include Supply, Wahiz, and Rendezvous 3.5. All of these maps have several vantage points, yet are somewhat simple providing for a perfect gameplay environment. By analyzing these maps, hopefully I will be able to fully understand what makes a very gameplay balanced map.

How comfortable are you with Avicus XML when it comes to creating it and analyzing it to fix possible errors?
-Not comfortable at all. Maybe if I saw another example of an XML, I would be able to fill in some parts. 

As builder, would you focus on building maps, creating XML, or both?
-I would focus on building maps and helping others build their maps. It's amazing to see all the potential people have with their maps in the community, and I want to do what I can to help as many as I can. 

Part 3: Past Experience

Provide the links for the threads of two maps that you have submitted to the Avicus forums.

-Plaza TE: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/d78444e99
*The map was updated more after this post and looks different than what you see in the Imgur album. It is currently in the map repository as well, so you can see the real thing if needed.

-Elevator: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/788315a84
*World download got corrupted.

-Dunebreak: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/a87ec31a6

-Map Veto Map: https://imgur.com/kS5a5bu

Have you had any past experience with building maps or creating XML, other than with the two maps linked above? If so, explain.
-Yes, I built some other maps such as this one: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/1f5f018b7

Other than that, I worked on some minor projects here and there either on my own or with others which eventually didn't get posted. I've ran across several ideas such as a Fusbol table in the form of a TDM.

Part 4: Self Reflection

Why do you want to be a builder?
-I want to be a builder so that I can have a safe and fast building environment. Often I get discouraged building when I have to do so many steps other than building the map itself such as collecting a world download, asking around for an XML etc.. I also want to learn how to improve on creating designs and making something look more visually appealing. Also, the map team seems to be needing a few more helping hands so any issues that I can fix that don't require a map developer, I'd be happy to fix! (Such as editing a coordinate in an XML, etc..)

How do you think you will help the map development team?
-I can help by providing feedback on people's maps. Back in early 2016, map developers almost never responded to maps until months later, but there were a few people who gave feedback on every single map release. I was one of those people who gave feedback when the map developers couldn't. I also hope that when there is a big project such as a tournament lobby or the main lobby, the stress is diverted and a big job becomes easier when the workload is shared. More recently, I will admit I haven't gave feedback on every single map, but I have on a few and have built a couple of more maps recently. 

This is my 2nd application, I have built a few more maps recently, so hopefully things work out this time?
